newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BankSA sees growth in SA business loan demand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BankSA sees growth in SA business loan demand.

text.p: BankSA Ltd managing director Terry Jay said on Friday he saw signs of growing confidence in South Australia, with the bank's commercial banking division seeing a 20 to 30 percent rise in loan applications on this time last year.

"We have got record levels of enquiries, we are writing very good business both from existing clients and new clients," he told journalists following the release of the bank's latest state and national economic surveys.

"Quietly our results show us some confidence ... a willingness to invest for the future that is stronger today than it has been," he said, noting interest was coming a lot from the rural sector but also from manufacturing.
Jay said the division, which covered property finance, business finance and leasing, rural and metropolitan, had met on Thursday.

"To a man, all would have said 20, 30 percent above where they were this time last year (for applications being processed)," he said, adding personal mortgage and personal loan areas were also showing good growth.
Jay said commercial business accounted for 50 percent of business for BankSA, a subsidiary of Advance Bank Australia Ltd.

In its survey on the SA economy, BankSA said there was a need to develop greater value-adding to the rural production, and risks for local manufacturing particularly if vehicle tariffs were wound back and the submarine project dried up.

BankSA Trends found the farm sector's share of the SA economy was 1.5 times the national average and manufacturing 1.2 times the national average, while mining's share was only half the national average but could rise on expansion of WMC Ltd's Olympic Dam project and the potential Gawler Craton gold region.

SA's construction industry was likely to continue to be smaller than the national average, as was the wholesale and retail trade sector, although the communications sector may improve through the multi-function polis and defence spending, it said.
